To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we measure a significant signal from the cross-correlation of galaxy clusters with the background galaxies, and that the signal is well described by a halo model with a mass-to-light ratio of ~300 h^(–1) M_sun/L_sun.
the mean radial profiles of clusters in the SDSS are detected over a wide range of scales, that the signal depends upon richness and luminosity, and that the profiles are not well fit by power laws.

the mean mass profiles of SDSS clusters scale strongly with richness, that the profiles depend upon luminosity, and that the mass-to-light ratios are consistent with the values measured in X-ray clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mass distribution of clusters, which has important implications for the evolution of the large-scale structure of the universe.
the weak gravitational lensing of SDSS galaxies by the large-scale structure.
measuring the weak lensing signal caused by clusters of galaxy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper is an excellent first step in a very interesting series.
the weak lensing signal from clusters is large and well measured, and that the signal is well fit by the halo model.
the cross-correlation signal is real, is detected at the 10% level, and scales with richness and luminous mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to measure the cluster-mass correlation function over a range of ~10^(–2)–10^(–1) h Mpc, and that it is well described by a halo model with a concentration-mass relation that is in good agreement with N-body simulations.
we have measured the mass profiles of clusters with a precision of ~10%.
clusters of galaxies have been shown to be an effective tool for weak lensing studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clusters are a rich source of cosmological information, and that the weak gravitational lensing of clusters is a powerful tool for extracting this information.
the cluster-mass correlation function is well measured over a wide range of scales.
clusters of galaxies are excellent probes of the large-scale structure of the Universe.
